newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Inkombank to sell ADRs to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Inkombank to sell ADRs to foreigners.

text.p: The Russian central bank has authorised AB Inkombank to sell American Depositary Receipts, the first time it has allowed a commercial bank to sell ADRs to foreign investors, Inkombank said on Monday.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has permitted Inkombank, Bank Vozrozhdeniye and Bank Menatep to issue Level One ADRs, but none of the paper has so far been issued as Russia's central bank does not allow foreigners to buy bank shares without its permission for each deal.

Inkombank will issue about 600,000 ADRs with one ADR covering 15 ordinary shares of the bank. Inkombank plans eventually to issue ADRs covering no more than three percent of its authorised capital, or nine million ordinary shares, it said in a statement.
Inkombank said its ordinary shares are now quoted at about $0.80, but like other banking shares are highly illiquid.
